advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide and document whether a lone '$' (not '$$' or '${') is a literal or an error; the current pass-through diverges from the stated '$$-to-escape' grammar.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/headers.py:111 docstring: "Otherwise any ``${`` begins a placeholder" and ":130 (write '$$' for a literal '$')"
A bare '$' (e.g. '$env:VAR}' with a missing opening brace, or 'a$b') is appended literally by the else-branch and never raises.
advisory.finding: A lone '$' that is not part of '$$' or '${' is silently passed through as a literal, but the module/substitute docstrings state the grammar requires '$$' to represent a literal '$' ('write $$ for a literal $'). A value like 'price$5' is accepted verbatim, which contradicts the stated escaping contract and could mask a mistyped placeholder (e.g. '$env:VAR}' missing a brace is emitted as-is rather than flagged).
scenarios: Operator writes '$env:VAR}' intending a placeholder but drops the '{'; it is emitted as a literal header value with no error.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reject the full illegal-field-value control-character range (C0 minus HTAB, plus DEL), not just CR/LF/NUL, in validate_header.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/headers.py:150-155 iterates only that map; any other control char in a substituted value is accepted.
advisory.finding: validate_header rejects only CR, LF and NUL in resolved values, but other C0 control characters (\x01–\x08, \x0b, \x0c, \x1f) and DEL (\x7f) are also illegal in RFC 7230 header field-values and can reach the value via ${env:VAR}. They pass validation and would be delivered as-is.
scenarios: An ${env:VAR} whose value contains a vertical tab or other C0 control char is accepted, though it is not a legal field-value character.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Detect header-name collisions that differ only by ASCII case within a single resolved map and raise LLMConfigError.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/headers.py:160-170: the loop stores `resolved[name] = substituted` with no case-folded collision check across entries.
JSON/TOML object keys are case-sensitive, so both 'X-Trace' and 'x-trace' survive as distinct dict keys.
advisory.finding: resolve_header_map validates each name/value entry independently and never detects two configured header names that differ only by case (e.g. 'X-Trace' and 'x-trace'). Both are stored in the returned dict; the vendor SDK merge behavior for case-variant duplicates is undefined, so one silently wins.
scenarios: Operator sets both 'X-Corp-Team' and 'x-corp-team' with different values; which one reaches the gateway depends on undefined SDK merge order.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a `headers` entry to the `[tool.rebar.llm]` block in docs/config.md (LLM framework section), mapping it to `REBAR_LLM_HEADERS`, alongside the existing `mcp_servers` sibling.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/config.py:530 adds `headers: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)` to LLMConfig, resolved via REBAR_LLM_HEADERS and `rebar -c llm.headers=` with the same three-layer precedence as mcp_servers (src/rebar/llm/config.py:670-676)
docs/config.md:395 documents the sibling knob `mcp_servers = {} # env REBAR_LLM_MCP_SERVERS (JSON); a TOML inline table in-file` inside the hand-authored [tool.rebar.llm] TOML block

docs/config.md:370-378 establishes this section as the maintained reference for the reserved `[tool.rebar.llm]` non-secret knobs resolved `rebar -c llm.KEY=VALUE` > `REBAR_LLM_<KEY>` env > config file > default
src/rebar/_config_schema.py:702-717 shows `llm` is absent from _SECTION_CLASSES, so config-reference.md (generated per docs/generated-artifacts.md:12) does not cover it — docs/config.md is the owner
search of docs/config.md for `headers` returned no matches
advisory.finding: docs/config.md's hand-authored [tool.rebar.llm] reference (the LLM framework section) is not updated for the new operator-configurable `headers` field / `REBAR_LLM_HEADERS` env var, so operators have no maintained documentation for this new configuration surface even though its established sibling `mcp_servers` is documented there.
scenarios: An operator wants to label gate LLM calls to an OpenAI-compatible gateway and looks up the [tool.rebar.llm] reference for the supported knob
advisory.suggested_fix: In docs/config.md's `[tool.rebar.llm]` TOML block (near line 395, beside `mcp_servers`), add a `headers = {} # env REBAR_LLM_HEADERS (JSON)` line and a short note describing the three-layer precedence and the ${env:...}/${run:...} value grammar (or link to rebar.llm.headers).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that a header name with a non-token character (e.g. `{"x t": "v"}`) raises LLMConfigError naming the RFC 7230 token set.
evidence: headers.py:146-149: `if not _TOKEN_RE.match(name): raise LLMConfigError(... 'contains characters outside the RFC 7230 token set')`

Named violating input: `REBAR_LLM_HEADERS='{"x t": "v"}'` (space is not an RFC 7230 token char) must raise LLMConfigError, but no test in test_llm_headers.py drives it — denied-name and negative-control tests all use valid token names.
search_files for `token` and `_TOKEN_RE` in tests/unit/test_llm_headers.py returned (no matches).
advisory.finding: The RFC 7230 token-set validation on header NAMES (validate_header, headers.py:146-149) has no test. Every test that reaches validate_header uses a well-formed token name; no test supplies a header name containing a character outside the RFC 7230 token set, so a regression that dropped or broke the `_TOKEN_RE.match(name)` guard would not be caught.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a parametrized test feeding invalid header names (space, `:`, control char, empty) via REBAR_LLM_HEADERS and asserting pytest.raises(LLMConfigError).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that a `[llm.headers]` TOML table with a non-string value (e.g. `"x-t" = 7`) raises LLMConfigError naming the layer.
evidence: headers.py:162-166: `if not isinstance(name, str) or not isinstance(value, str): raise LLMConfigError(f"{layer}: header entries must be string name/value pairs; ...")`
headers.py:222-223: file-table dict path `if isinstance(file_value, dict): return resolve_header_map(file_value, ...)` reaches this guard.

Named violating input: rebar.toml with `[llm.headers]\n"x-t" = 7` — a native TOML table whose value is an int — must raise, but test_file_table_bad_shape_raises only covers `headers = 7` and `headers = "[1,2]"` (the outer non-table/non-object shapes), not a valid table with a non-string entry.
advisory.finding: The non-string name/value type-guard in resolve_header_map (headers.py:162-166) has no test. It is reachable via the native-TOML-table dict path (resolve_headers line 222-223), where a TOML value can be a non-string (int/array), but no test supplies a header table with a non-string value or non-string key.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test writing `[llm.headers]\n"x-t" = 7` to rebar.toml and asserting pytest.raises(LLMConfigError, match="string name/value").
